Henck Arron was a Surinamese banker and politician who led the country to independence in 1975 and was its first prime minister, until the army overthrew him in 1980.

Leader of the mainly Creole National Party of Suriname, he became premier in 1973 and pressed for independence, which the Netherlands was keen to grant. The Hindustani party feared it and opposed it, and the fear helped drive the exodus to the Netherlands.

His government was accused of corruption and of neglecting the army. On 25 February 1980 sergeants led by Dési Bouterse seized power, and Arron was briefly imprisoned. He later returned to politics as vice-president from 1988 to 1990. He is remembered as the father of Suriname's independence.
sum: Henck Arron was a Surinamese banker and politician who led the country to independence in 1975 and was its first prime minister, until the army overthrew him in 1980.
